hook.text: Writing a payroll program is easy. The rules are known, so you simply code them.

hook2.text: But what are the rules for recognising speech? People do it every day, and nobody can explain how.

learn.text: So we let the computer learn from examples. Machine learning optimises a performance criterion, using example data or past experience.

model.text: What it learns is a model: a useful approximation, not the perfect truth.

sup.text: The first kind of learning has a teacher. Every example comes with the right answer. That is supervised learning.

cls.text: A bank knows each customer's income and savings, and whether they were low risk or high risk. Learning finds the thresholds that separate them. The answer is a class, so this is classification.

reg.text: Now predict a used car's price from its mileage. The answer is a number, so this is regression. Learning finds the line.

unsup.text: Take the answers away. Only the inputs are left. That is unsupervised learning.

clus.text: The learner can still find groups of similar examples, like customer segments. These groups are clusters, not classes. Nobody has named them.

rl.text: The third kind is reinforcement learning. A robot in a maze gets no answer for each step. It gets a reward only at the end.

rl2.text: From that delayed reward, it learns a policy: which move to make, in every place.

assoc.text: Week one also finds associations. Of ten baskets with a computer, seven also hold a mouse. So the probability of a mouse, given a computer, is zero point seven.

par.text: One last idea. Some learners fix the form of the answer before they see any data. They are parametric.

par2.text: The line, y equals w x plus w zero, is parametric. Its shape is chosen in advance. Learning only fills in w and w zero. More data never changes the form.

npar.text: A nonparametric learner has no such fixed formula. A decision tree's questions, and how deep it grows, come from the data itself.

ex1.text: Supervised: every example has its answer.

ex2.text: Classification gives a class. Regression gives a number.

ex4.text: Reinforcement learns a policy from a delayed reward.

ex5.text: Parametric fixes the form. Nonparametric does not.
